column1: # install-topology-known-red.tsv — shipped suites accepted as red under the version-keyed
# install topology that tools/install-topology-selftest.sh stages.
# A suite listed here is REPORT-ONLY. A suite NOT listed here that fails or times out is a red
# build. A listed suite that PASSES is a warning, never a red — that is the "shrink the list"
# direction, the same contract tools/mutation-baseline.tsv carries for survivors. A row that
# matches no staged suite is a stale-row warning, also never a red. So a fix and the removal of
# its row do not have to land in the same commit.
# TAB-separated. Columns:
#   repo-relative path <TAB> cause
# The key is the REPO-relative path (`plugins/<name>/<rel>`), NOT the staged one: a staged path
# carries a version segment, so keying on it would rot every row at the next release.
# EVERY ROW STATES ITS CAUSE. A row whose cause is not actually known reads `undiagnosed` —
# an admission, visibly, rather than an invented rationale that reads like an exemption.
# Draining this list is tracked in #421.
# SOME ROWS ARE ENVIRONMENT-DEPENDENT, and those say so in their cause. A suite whose failure
# depends on the bash version or on which CLIs are installed will PASS on some machines, and
# the guard will then warn "listed known-red but PASSED — drop its row". Do NOT act on that
# warning from a single green run: read the cause first, and drop the row only once the suite
# passes in the environment the cause names. The two rows added after the first CI run are
# exactly this kind, and they are why the seeding number below has two figures rather than one.
# Seeded from the guard's first run on the authoring machine — 55 suites, 51 pass, 4 listed —
# and CORRECTED by the first run in a second environment, which is the only kind that can
# falsify a "measured here" claim: CI scores 49 pass, 6 listed on both lanes. The two extra
# rows were real failures the authoring machine's environment hid. plan-lint-selftest.sh and
# design-sync-selftest.mjs are deliberately ABSENT — both were fixed rather than listed, and
# so was workflows-mjs-selftest.sh, which was red only because it invokes design-sync's.
plugins/review-toolkit/scripts/check-emit-deadline-selftest.sh
column2: check-emit-deadline.sh derives REPO as $HERE/../../.. and globs $REPO/plugins/*/agents; from an install that is the cache root, so zero agents are linted and four assertions expecting named agents fail.

column1: plugins/second-shift/skills/doctor/tools/doctor-selftest.sh
column2: resolves its review-toolkit sibling as $HERE/../../../../review-toolkit, a fixed hop count that only holds in the monorepo, so the resolved scenario degrades into the unresolved one.

column1: plugins/dev-pipeline/skills/run/tools/preflight-selftest.sh
column2: preflight-selftest.sh:38 resolves its review-toolkit sibling as $SCRIPT_DIR/../../../../review-toolkit, a fixed hop count that only holds in the monorepo. From an install SECOND_SHIFT_REVIEW_TOOLKIT_ROOT is empty, so preflight.sh:144-147 falls through to its `claude plugin list` rung. ENVIRONMENT-DEPENDENT: that rung hits where the Claude CLI is installed, so the suite passes on a developer machine and fails on CI. Reproduced by removing `claude` from PATH, not by re-running.

column1: plugins/dev-pipeline/skills/run/tools/cost-block-selftest.sh
column2: cost-block-selftest.sh:40 mirrors pipeline-cost-block.sh state resolution but anchors it on $HERE, while the script anchors on $PWD; in an install cache $HERE has no git repo above it, so the mirror falls to `cd ""`. ENVIRONMENT-DEPENDENT on what bash does with that: a silent no-op on bash <= 5.2 (STATE_DIR lands inside the staged plugin, where the script never looks, and the three dump assertions get no rollup JSON) and an error on bash >= 5.3 (STATE_DIR collapses to ./ and coincidentally agrees with the script). Red on both CI lanes, green on bash 5.3.
